column1: # Where every agent skill comes from. One row per skill, TSV, '# ' comments.
#           spec = GitHub repository that owns the skill. Linked from a checkout
#           when one exists (so it updates with `git pull`), otherwise fetched
#           with `npx skills add <repo> --skill <id> -g`. The CLI does not
#           discover every layout, so a clone is the reliable path.
#   dagr    owned by the herdr-dagr plugin. Extracted with `dagr --skill` into
#           that plugin's own skills/ directory (next to its examples/), then
#           linked. spec = herdr plugin id that provides the dagr binary.
#   bundle  no installable home exists, so this repo is the source of truth.
#           spec = path in this repo, and it points into home/ because that is
#           where the mirror of ~/.agents/skills lives. This is debt: the `why`
#           says what would let it be deleted, and scripts/skills-sync.sh reports
# All of them live in one repository, each in its own top-level directory with
# its own pyproject/Makefile. They are NOT in skills/ and `npx skills add` does not
# find them (verified: "No valid skills found"), so the only reliable install is
# A checkout at <root>/mycord takes precedence over the skills under
# ~/.agents/skills, because the repo carries .env.example and the current text
# while the copies there have drifted. If you already keep the skills there as
# hand-copies, see docs/mycord.md for the one-time cleanup.

column4: This repo's own install/configure/upgrade guide; home is this repo by definition.
Apothic-AI/one-shot-genius exists but is empty (0 bytes, no commits), so `npx skills add` cannot fetch it yet. Becomes kind=repo once the skill is pushed.

Fork of the skill `herdr --skill` ships: ~56 delta lines, mostly target-verification-before-delegation, which this orchestration setup depends on. Rebase onto the shipped file when herdr changes and send the delta upstream; becomes kind=shipped when herdr takes it.

Owned by the herdr-dagr plugin pinned in herdr/plugins.toml. Never bundle: `dagr --skill` is byte-identical to the plugin's own copy, so a bundled copy is a silent fork of a file the plugin already owns.
Owned by our fork, which ships skills/unblock/SKILL.md. The fork's copy is newer than any bundled copy (it documents queue-page sign-in), so bundling would freeze agents on a stale skill.

Routing skill for the whole library: which medium exists, which are planned, and to install the medium's own skill before writing code. Install this one first; it is the index the comms agent reads to choose.
The comms space's Discord surface (discord.py-self REPL). User-account automation: violates Discord's ToS and can get the account banned - never initiate unprompted.
The comms space's Telegram surface (Telethon REPL). Supports real user accounts; Telegram permits third-party clients.
The comms space's Slack surface: drives Slack as the signed-in human via an xoxc- client token plus the httpOnly `d` cookie, with no app registration.
The comms space's IRC surface (pydle REPL), TLS by default.

The comms space's Signal surface: drives Signal as the signed-in human through signal-cli's JSON-RPC daemon (no bot, no app registration) and carries 1:1 call audio as raw PCM over a per-call Unix socket; refuses the call path loudly on a stale version pin instead of failing mid-call.

The comms space's Zoom surface: joins the desktop client via its own `zoommtg://` URL scheme (no account, no SDK app), speaks into the meeting with Piper TTS and captures the speaker output with an energy VAD through a PipeWire/PulseAudio virtual device plane.

Guides creating, editing and deleting pi-profile-switch profiles. Named by every `leader`/`worker` profile's `skills` list, so it must exist on any machine that can run a lane — and it was the one skill in the agent-dir root that was still a hand copy rather than a link.
The comms space's email surface: Himalaya CLI with a per-account wrapper config.
The comms space's SMS/voice surface (unofficial gvoice TS client). Reading works; sending SMS needs a captured exchange.

Drives a Ferdium install over CDP: launches it headless on a virtual display or headed, discovers per-service webviews, and reads or interacts with any of them. The catch-all for a service with no dedicated skill.
Host-specific half of the shared Fly build box: provisioning, the idle supervisor and scale-to-zero. The build-side half is the cargo-remote-build skill in the cargo-remote-3000 repo.
Fleet scheduling with agents-cron: the systemd timer, task registry, run artifacts and failure semantics. Delivered only as a repo skill — no pi package ships it, so a package sweep cannot see it.
Durable project task tracking with bd: ready work, claim/close, dependency blockers, multi-session handoff. Delivered only as a repo skill.
Token and context conservation: measure before reading, keyhole inspection, and construct every wait to fire on failure as well as success. Delivered only as a repo skill.
How a lane's name is derived and where it must match — herdr agent name, PI_ROOMS_NAME, dagr owner, all from the tab label at spawn. Delivered only as a repo skill.
The pi-goal completion contract: goal_complete/goal_blocked/goal_wait and the queue verbs. Delivered only as a repo skill.
Policy-only memory retrieval: memory_search and session_search before work that depends on durable context. Delivered only as a repo skill.
How pi-persist injects text into every request: the cached section channel versus the trailing channel. Delivered only as a repo skill.
Agent messaging rules: stable name pins, the two delivery states, and rooms_dm versus a herdr prompt. Delivered only as a repo skill.

How to drive the shared Fly build box: dispatch a build, poll it, and read the log. It ships no pi package and lives in no pi registry, so a package sweep cannot see it; before this row it existed only as a hand-made link into a ~/Code checkout. Now declared against the in-tree copy, which is the same commit.
